projects.summary: Optivision is a comprehensive B2B CRM and ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) solution designed to enable optical stores to manage their customer, prescription, order, financial, and inventory processes end-to-end.
projects.slug: By digitising businesses’ paperwork, it enables them to create prescriptions, track customer accounts and view income and expenditure analyses in a matter of seconds.
projects.title: OPTIVISON
projects.description:
# **Key Features**

Comprehensive Prescription and Order Management: Accurate digital recording and tracking of customers’ eye measurement values (spherical, cylindrical, axis, etc.).

* **Finance and Accounts Receivable Module:** Real-time monitoring of the business’s income-expense balance and customer-based credit/debt records.
* **Telegram Integration:** Automatic delivery of critical notifications and daily summary reports to the business owner’s Telegram account.
* **Advanced Authentication (Auth):** Secure user login and role-based access management using Supabase Auth.
* **Modern and Responsive Interface:** Dark Mode support, “Premium” login animations, and mobile-responsive design.

##  **Technical Architecture and Technologies Used**

This project is built using a scalable, performance-focused architecture that adheres to current industry standards:

### **Frontend Technologies:**

* **React 18 & TypeScript:** A modular architecture enhanced with robust type safety, a goal of zero “runtime errors,” and modern React hooks.
* **Vite:** An ultra-fast bundler preferred over Webpack, offering instant HMR (Hot Module Replacement).
* **State Management:** TanStack Query (React Query) was used for asynchronous data fetching, caching, and optimistic UI updates.
* **UI & CSS:** Tailwind CSS was integrated for a utility-first approach, along with customizable shadcn/ui components (Radix UI) that comply with accessibility (a11y) standards. Form management and validation were handled using React Hook Form + Zod.
* **Data Visualization:** Recharts was used to dynamically plot financial metrics.

### Backend & Database:

**Supabase:** A PostgreSQL-based database infrastructure. Database-level security was ensured through Row Level Security (RLS) rules. Real-time database listening features enabled instant updates.

### Deployment and DevOps Processes

The project has been designed with an isolated architecture to ensure it runs with the same stability across all environments:

* **Docker:** The application has been containerized using a Dockerfile and compiled to run on a lightweight Nginx image (Alpine). This completely eliminates dependency issues.
* **VPS and Reverse Proxy:** The project has been deployed on an Ubuntu-based VPS using Docker Compose. A primary Nginx layer has been positioned as a reverse proxy in front of the server, and incoming HTTP requests are routed to the underlying containers.
* **CI/CD Setup:** The project’s GitHub repository has been prepared for an infrastructure where Docker images will be automatically built via GitHub Actions and pushed to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).



### Highlights:

* **Type Safety:** By using TypeScript interfaces and types throughout the codebase, runtime errors have been prevented and code readability has been improved.
* **Modern State Management:** Instead of cumbersome structures like Redux, TanStack Query was successfully implemented by clearly separating server-state and client-state.
* **Component-Oriented Architecture:** Reusable and isolated React components (Dashboard, Orders, Revenue) compliant with SOLID principles were created under the \`components/\` directory.
* **Real-World Problem Solving:** This project is not just a “To-Do app” clone; it is a working product that solves the complex business logic (prescription math, debt management) of a real-world business in the optical industry.
